subject: Regression with missing predictors in Lavaan

messages.author: 1893408bac431331
messages.subject: Regression with missing predictors in Lavaan
parts:
Hi, I want to do regression with lavaan when data contains missing values - but it is giving an error that I can not figure out. Any help will be really appreciated

Here is the code:
rm(list=ls())
n = 10
p = 5
x = matrix(rnorm(n*p),n,p)
beta = rep(0,p)
beta[1:4] = rnorm(4)
y = rnorm(1) + x %*% beta + 0.25*rnorm(n)
colnames(x) = paste("x",1:ncol(x),sep="")
colnames(y) = paste("y",1:ncol(y),sep="")
x[sample(prod(dim(x)),0.1*prod(dim(x)))] = NA

library(lavaan)
my.model = paste(colnames(y),' ~ ',paste(colnames(x),collapse=" + "),sep="")
run = lavaan(my.model,data=as.data.frame(cbind(y,x)),model.type="sem",missing='fiml')

output:
Error in lav_model_estimate(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  : 
  lavaan ERROR: initial model-implied matrix (Sigma) is not positive definite;
  check your model and/or starting parameters.
In addition: Warning message:
In lav_partable_check(lavpartable) :
  lavaan WARNING: missing intercepts are set to zero: [y1]

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: Regression with missing predictors in Lavaan
parts: You need a variance for your outcome variable.  Try:
my.model = paste(colnames(y),' ~ ',paste(colnames(x),collapse=" + "),sep="")

my.model <- paste0(my.model, "\n y1 ~~ y1")

Incidentally, the code to build your model is longer and harder to read than your model. Why not:

my.model <- "y1 ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5
 y1 ~~ y1"

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Regression with missing predictors in Lavaan
parts:
The residual variance of the outcome would be estimated automatically (as would your "missing intercepts") if you used the sem() function instead of the lavaan() function.

Terry

messages.subject: Re: Regression with missing predictors in Lavaan
parts:
Thanks alot Jeremy and Terry! This works! 

But when I increase the number of variables more than the number of observations, the model runs for a few EM iterations and then crashes with a positive definite error for the covariance. I tried with different missing and estimator options (direct/ml/fiml) but none seems to work. Is there any approximate/other way to compute the model in such a case.

@Jeremy, I wrote the model in the complex formulation so that I can play with 'p'.

Script:
rm(list=ls())
n = 10
p = 20

x = matrix(rnorm(n*p),n,p)
beta = rep(0,p)
beta[1:4] = rnorm(4)
y = rnorm(1) + x %*% beta + 0.25*rnorm(n)
colnames(x) = paste("x",1:ncol(x),sep="")
colnames(y) = paste("y",1:ncol(y),sep="")
x[sample(prod(dim(x)),0.1*prod(dim(x)))] = NA
library(lavaan)
my.model = paste(colnames(y),' ~ ',paste(colnames(x),collapse=" + "),sep="")

run = sem(my.model,data=as.data.frame(cbind(y,x)),missing='fiml',verbose=TRUE) #with lavaan() function use: "y1 ~~ y1"

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Regression with missing predictors in Lavaan
parts: On 01/07/2015 10:42 AM, Suleiman Khan wrote:

> Error in chol.default(S) :
> the leading minor of order 16 is not positive definite

In dev 0.5-18.763, I now use ridging (= adding a small constant to the
diagonal of sigma) to avoid this. It may work, but it is far from an
elegant solution.

Usually, a Bayesian approach is used in the 'small n, large p' setting.
But I have no time to investigate this now.

Yves.
